newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-WEIR'S TOUR IN DOUBT AFTER KICKING INCIDENT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WEIR'S TOUR IN DOUBT AFTER KICKING INCIDENT.

text.p: Lock Doddie Weir may miss the remainder of the British Lions' tour of South Africa after being kicked in the knee during the tourists emphatic victory over Mpumalanga on Wednesday.
Lions coach Ian McGeechan was so incensed by the incident -- in which Marius Bosman was clearly seen kicking Weir's left knee during a maul -- that he considered citing the player.

McGeechan said after his side's 64-14 victory: "I did say I planned to cite the player but I understand from International Rugby Board regulations and from the agreement on this tour we cannot cite if the referee takes action as he did on this occasion.
"I was very disappointed by the incident. It wasn't in the context of the game and unfortunately something as cold blooded as that may have ended a Lions tour for Doddie."
Weir is feared to have medial ligament damage although it will be 24 hours before his fate is properly known.

Referee Carl Spannenberg awarded a penalty to the Lions following the incident and took similar action when a touch judge reported lock Elandre van der Bergh for stamping on flanker Rob Wainwright's head.

Wainwright was not injured in the incident, unlike England full-back Jonathan Callard who required 25 stitches to his face after the same player stamped on him in England's match against Eastern Province on their tour three years ago.
Gert Grobler, the Mpumalanga manager, said neither act had been intentional but he would study the video and take action if necessary.
McGeechan added: "If somebody has rugby at heart they would be responsible for their players and if they take action we would be very pleased."
The incidents soured a match in which the Lions produced their best rugby in four tour matches to date.
